answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake that grows with every extra identity it claims, so spinning up a nebula of fake agents becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation then accrues slowly through completed, verified work, like a juniper adding one ring at a time, never granted at signup. An attacker chasing the zenith of influence must fund each fake identity and wait out the same slow climb, so the cost of faking scale exceeds any reward.
